notes:
Task and constraints: Count the asterisks that are not inside any pair of '|' characters.
Idea: Track whether the scan is outside bars, toggle state at each `|`, and count `*` only while outside.
Technique and why it applies: Toggling at each bar distinguishes asterisks inside sections from those outside.
Invariant: The boolean state alternates at each delimiter and accurately marks whether the current character is inside a paired-bar section.
Edge cases: Asterisks between bars are ignored; input guarantees paired bars.
Complexity: O(n) time and O(1) space.
complexity_reason: Toggling at each bar distinguishes asterisks inside sections from those outside.

notes:
Task and constraints: Return true if both diagonals contain only nonzero values and all other cells are zero.
Idea: For every cell, require nonzero values on either diagonal and zero everywhere else.
Technique and why it applies: Index equations identify diagonal cells and enforce the complementary zero requirement.
Invariant: The row and column indices determine whether a cell belongs to either diagonal.
Edge cases: The center cell of an odd-sized matrix belongs to both diagonals but is checked once; zero is forbidden on diagonals.
Complexity: O(n²) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity_reason: Index equations identify diagonal cells and enforce the complementary zero requirement.

notes:
Task and constraints: Decode message using the first-occurrence order of letters in key, preserving spaces.
Idea: Build a substitution map from each distinct non-space key letter in first-occurrence order to `a` through `z`, then decode message while preserving spaces.
Technique and why it applies: First-occurrence order defines the cipher mapping, and direct lookup decodes each message letter.
Invariant: The mapping is assigned only on a letter's first appearance and remains fixed during decoding.
Edge cases: Spaces are copied unchanged; repeated key letters do not consume new mappings; message letters are lowercase.
Complexity: O(|key|+|message|) time and O(1) alphabet-map space apart from output.
complexity_reason: First-occurrence order defines the cipher mapping, and direct lookup decodes each message letter.

notes:
Task and constraints: Evaluate a binary tree whose leaves are 0/1 and whose internal nodes represent OR (2) or AND (3).
Idea: Recursively return false or true for leaf values 0 or 1; evaluate both children and combine with OR for value 2 or AND for value 3.
Technique and why it applies: Postorder evaluation obtains child values before applying the parent operator.
Invariant: Each recursive call returns the boolean value represented by its subtree.
Edge cases: Leaves have no children; internal nodes use only the defined OR and AND operators.
Complexity: O(n) time and O(h) recursion space.
complexity_reason: Postorder evaluation obtains child values before applying the parent operator.

notes:
Task and constraints: Return the minimum seconds needed to fill all cups, filling two different types per second when possible.
Idea: Return the maximum of the largest amount and the ceiling of half the total amount.
Technique and why it applies: The lower bounds from the largest pile and two-at-a-time capacity together give the optimum.
Invariant: Each second can serve at most two different types, and the largest pile needs at least its own number of seconds.
Edge cases: Zero total returns zero; integer ceiling is `(sum+1)//2` or `(sum+1)/2`.
Complexity: O(1) time and O(1) space for three cup types.
complexity_reason: The lower bounds from the largest pile and two-at-a-time capacity together give the optimum.

notes:
Task and constraints: Return the number of equal-value pairs and the number of leftover elements.
Idea: Count frequencies and sum each frequency divided by two; leftovers equal array length minus twice the pair count.
Technique and why it applies: Frequency halves count all possible equal pairs, and the remaining length gives leftovers.
Invariant: Each value contributes one pair for every two occurrences, leaving at most one unpaired occurrence.
Edge cases: Duplicate values can form multiple pairs; no pair crosses distinct values.
Complexity: O(n+U) time and O(U) frequency space, where U is the value range.
complexity_reason: Frequency halves count all possible equal pairs, and the remaining length gives leftovers.

notes:
Task and constraints: Classify a five-card hand as Flush, Three of a Kind, Pair, or High Card.
Idea: Check for a flush first; otherwise count ranks and return Three of a Kind, Pair, or High Card according to maximum frequency.
Technique and why it applies: Testing flush before rank counts follows the poker-hand category priority.
Invariant: Flush takes precedence; without it, maximum rank frequency uniquely determines the remaining category.
Edge cases: A five-card hand is assumed; three matching ranks outrank a pair; suit equality is checked across all cards.
Complexity: O(1) time and O(1) space for five cards and bounded ranks.
complexity_reason: Testing flush before rank counts follows the poker-hand category priority.

notes:
Task and constraints: Return the first character whose second occurrence is encountered while scanning left to right.
Idea: Scan left to right using a set or 26-slot boolean array; return immediately when the current character has already been seen.
Technique and why it applies: A seen lookup identifies the first character whose second occurrence is reached.
Invariant: Before each character, the seen structure contains exactly the characters in the preceding prefix.
Edge cases: The first repeated encounter is returned; input guarantees a repeated character for the problem.
Complexity: O(n) time and O(1) space for lowercase letters.
complexity_reason: A seen lookup identifies the first character whose second occurrence is reached.

notes:
Task and constraints: Return the minimum number of operations required to make every array element zero.
Idea: Count distinct positive values; each distinct positive level requires one subtraction operation.
Technique and why it applies: Each operation removes one distinct positive level, so the number of levels is minimal.
Invariant: The set or boolean table contains every positive value that needs to be eliminated at a distinct stage.
Edge cases: Zeros need no operation; repeated positive values are removed together; an all-zero array returns zero.
Complexity: O(n+U) time and O(U) space for a bounded domain, or O(u) set space.
complexity_reason: Each operation removes one distinct positive level, so the number of levels is minimal.

notes:
Task and constraints: Merge weights for matching item values and return value-weight pairs sorted by value.
Idea: Sum weights by item value in a map, then emit entries ordered by value using sorting or `TreeMap`.
Technique and why it applies: Aggregating by value combines duplicates, and ordered iteration satisfies the required output order.
Invariant: The aggregate for each value equals its weight total across both input lists.
Edge cases: Values appearing in both lists are merged; output values are ascending and each appears once.
Complexity: O((n+m) log u) time with sorting or ordered map operations and O(u) space.
complexity_reason: Aggregating by value combines duplicates, and ordered iteration satisfies the required output order.
